rounds.proof_sketch: N=2048, TILE_SIZE=32, gridDim.x=(2048+31)/32=64, max blockIdx.x=63, max col=63*32+31=2047. Since max col=2047<N=2048, the condition col<N is always true when col reaches maximum. The mutation col<=N would only differ if col==N=2048, but no thread ever computes col=2048.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutant changes the write-back guard from `col < N` to `col <= N`. For this to matter, a thread must have col == N. With N=2048 and TILE_SIZE=32, the grid has gridDim.x = 64 blocks, giving blockIdx.x in [0,63] and threadIdx.x in [0,31]. Maximum col = 63*32+31 = 2047 = N-1. Since N is exactly divisible by TILE_SIZE, the grid covers exactly indices [0, N-1] with no overflow. No thread ever computes col=N, so `col < N` and `col <= N` evaluate identically for all threads.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under this configuration. The mutation only differs when col==N, but with N=2048 being an exact multiple of TILE_SIZE=32, the maximum col is N-1=2047. Would need N to not be a multiple of TILE_SIZE (e.g., N=2049) to expose the bug, but shapes are fixed.
rounds.recommendations: When testing boundary-condition mutations in tiled GPU kernels, verify whether the dimension is an exact multiple of tile size. If it is, boundary guard mutations (< vs <=) may be unreachable. Include test cases where dimensions are NOT exact multiples of tile sizes to improve mutation coverage.
